summary.headline: SS Retail Q2 FY27 revenue rose 87% YoY to INR940 crore and PAT 160% to INR28 crore, with H1 SSG at 38%.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT for Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue up 87% YoY to INR940 crore and EBITDA up 99% to INR52.4 crore at a 5.6% margin. Gross margin rose 71 bps to 12.7% in Q2, helped by OEM margins and lower discounting as prices rose. Growth was driven about equally by ASP (roughly 35%) and volume (roughly 35-37%) in H1. Management reiterated 750 stores by FY28 and doubling revenue from the FY26 base, with a 35-40% SSG guidance for the year.

financial_highlights.value: 46% in Q2 FY27; 38% in H1 FY27

segments.name: Mobile phones
segments.commentary: 86% of Q2 FY27 revenue. Samsung and Apple together about 50% of mobile revenue, balance Chinese brands; Apple share may fall 2-3% in H2 on delayed launches.

segments.name: Pre-owned smartphones (Mobile Exchange Wala)
segments.commentary: 7.3% of Q2 revenue vs 6.5% in the prior quarter; operating in 108 stores (vs 71 in FY26), under 20% of the 574-store network. Target about 30% penetration by FY29; inventory around 40 days.

segments.name: Accessories and protection
segments.commentary: About 5% of Q2 revenue; management flagged it as a high-margin category to scale.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Maharashtra about 92% of revenue (94% last year); non-Maharashtra 8% in Q2 vs 6% a year earlier. H1 growth: metros 118%, urban 58%, rural 69%.

segments.name: Olineo and Nexora (new subsidiaries)
segments.commentary: About INR40 crore in Q2 (about 6% of revenue) vs about INR28 crore in Q1; EBITDA margin described as neutral to low.

guidance_outlook: Revenue to double from the FY26 base by FY28; store network to reach 750 by FY28 (about 250 new stores over FY27-FY28 from 503 base).
FY27 SSG guidance of 35-40%; ASP growth to slow to about 10-15% next year, with double-digit SSG expected in FY28.
Gross margin expected at 13% and above over the next 18-24 months as direct OEM purchasing phases in over 12-18 months.

EBITDA margin expected to expand as new stores mature; management pointed to 6% EBITDA margin as the aspirational level in the presentation. New stores run at about 4-4.5% EBITDA margin; mature stores above 5%.
PAT margin expected to rise another 20-30 bps in H2 FY27 as IPO proceeds reduce working capital borrowing; interest cost to fall from 0.6-0.7x toward 0.3-0.4x.
Advertising spend planned at about 0.35% of revenue in FY27 vs 0.25-0.3% last year; capex about INR15 lakh per store, around INR20 crore for FY27 and similar for FY28.
capex_capacity: Store network 574 across 228 cities and five states, about 2.8 lakh sq ft; 38 stores added in Q2 FY27 and 71 in H1 FY27 (about 65% of the 120-store FY27 target already added).
Store capex about INR15 lakh per store; around INR20 crore for FY27 and similar for FY28.
About 70% of stores are in Tier 2, Tier 3 and smaller towns.
Chhattisgarh operations started in Q3 FY27; management said it would announce details next quarter. Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Haryana flagged as future entries, about one new state per year.
Inventory at INR583 crore in H1 FY27 vs INR341 crore a year ago; inventory days 54 (vs 46-47 earlier), guided to 46-50 days and below 50 by end-Q3.
demand_pricing: Industry: mobile prices up about 20% with premiumisation; volumes down about 15%, with the drop concentrated in sub-INR15,000 phones. Management expects the industry to grow faster than 10% this year.
Company ASP including GST rose to about INR34,050 in H1 FY27 from INR25,513 in H1 FY26 (about 33%). H1 volume growth about 3%-37% by different accounts, with ASP contributing about 35%.
Apple demand held in H1; softer in H2 in volume terms only (base models down, Pro series up 1.5-1.8x per management). Management said value impact is limited because Apple prices rose 15-20%.
Nearly 70% of sales financed by consumer finance; over 60% of customers are repeat buyers (tracked on stores older than three years).
Competition: management says e-commerce share is declining in electronics and quick commerce is not a threat, citing look-and-feel, exchange and two-year warranty offers.
Margin bridge for H1 gross margin gain: about 50% from OEM margin increases and about 50% from lower discounting in a price-hike environment.

qa_highlights.question: What SSG and Gujarat/other-market contribution are built into the doubling-revenue plan?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 growth of 73% already; H2 expected slightly higher than H1, consistent with the 45-47% / 53-55% seasonal split. SSG guided at 35-40%. Maharashtra share to fall below 90% after FY28; out-of-Maharashtra mix to fall 2-3% per year for the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Can Mobile Exchange Wala reach 30% penetration and what is inventory holding?
qa_highlights.answer: Penetration is 20% now (108 of 574 stores) and is targeted at 30% by FY29. Pre-owned needs no hub stock, with about 40 days of inventory vs roughly 7 weeks for new devices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 SSG figure, given 38% in the press release vs 46% in remarks?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 SSG was about 46% and H1 about 38%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to a 6% EBITDA margin and gross margin upside?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin could reach 13%+ as direct OEM purchasing phases in. EBITDA margin should rise as stores mature; new stores run about 4-4.5% and mature stores above 5%. Management said better OEM margins would offset lower discounting gains.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow faster than revenue in H1, and is there operating leverage in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 20 bps higher DBD (finance-related) charges as finance share rose to about 70% from 55-57%, plus higher partner commissions tied to Olineo (FOFO) and partner incentives. Commissions expected to stabilise, so some operating leverage is expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up sharply in H1, and will it fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose about 80% to INR583 crore (from INR341 crore) vs revenue up 73%, reflecting festive stocking. Days expected to stay in a 46-50 day range, with a minimum of about five weeks at stores and 1.5-2 weeks at hubs.

qa_highlights.question: Non-Maharashtra revenue share and new-state plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Maharashtra share was 8% in Q2 (6% a year earlier); the earlier 12% figure cited by an analyst was not confirmed. No new state this year beyond Chhattisgarh, which started in Q3; one new state planned per year after that.

risks_watch: Gross margin depends on OEM terms; management said H1 gains were roughly half OEM and half lower discounting, and lower discounting may not repeat.
New-state expansion (about 50% of new stores outside Maharashtra) could dilute EBITDA margin during the 1-2 year break-even period.
Volume is falling in sub-INR15,000 phones; Apple volumes softer in H2 with delayed launches.
Inventory days at 54 vs 46-47 a year ago; working capital and DBD/finance-related costs rising.
Olineo and Nexora are new (about six months old) with low margins; their contribution (about 6% of revenue) needs tracking.
Management said the ASP rise (about 35%) will slow to 10-15% next year, which reduces price-led SSG and shifts growth to volume.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and demand; more specific on store and SSG targets than on margin path. Management gave a 6% EBITDA aspiration without a firm timeline and answered some questions loosely (e.g., Q2 SSG figure, non-Maharashtra share), so treat qualitative margin and interest-cost comments with caution.
key_quotes: Q2 FY27 has been an extraordinary encouraging quarter for us, with the company delivering its highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, and PAT.
We are pretty confident that this year also, the behavior will be very similar.
Our focus is not simply on adding stores, but on ensuring that every store we add continues meaningfully to the strength and profitability of overall business.

adds.what: Retail store network additions: 250 new stores over FY27-FY28 from 503 base (targeting 750 by FY28); 71 added in H1 FY27, 38 in Q2 FY27
Chhattisgarh state entry (operations started Q3 FY27, details to be announced)

growth.why: Management reiterates 750 stores by FY28 (250 openings from a 503 base, 71 done in H1 FY27) and doubling FY26 revenue by FY28, with FY27 SSG guided at 35-40%; store capex (~INR15 lakh each, ~INR20 crore FY27) is specified but the revenue doubling target lacks a modelled bridge, and growth relies on ASP and SSG, so backing is partial.

oneOffs.what: H1 ASP up ~33-35% (INR25,513 to INR34,050) passed through as price-led growth; ASP rise expected to slow to 10-15% next year
About 50% of H1 gross margin gain (~30-40 bps) from lower discounting in a price-hike environment, which may not repeat
Olineo and Nexora new subsidiaries contributed about INR40 crore (~6% of Q2 revenue), up from about INR28 crore in Q1, at neutral to low margins

quality.why: Q2 revenue rose 87% with H1 growth split roughly evenly between ASP (~35%) and volume (~35-37%, though brief quotes H1 volume at 3%-37% across accounts), so a large share is price-led and that ASP tailwind is set to slow to 10-15% next year; the brief gives no explicit one-off gains, but the ASP pass-through and discount-driven margin gain are non-recurring in nature.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin guided at 13%+ over 18-24 months as direct OEM buying phases in, and EBITDA margin expected to rise as stores mature (new stores ~4-4.5%, mature >5%), though H1 EBITDA margin was flat at 5.6% and the 6% level is only an aspiration without timeline.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 71 stores added in H1 FY27 (about 65% of the 120-store FY27 target), with 250 openings planned over FY27-FY28 from a 503 base to reach 750, backed by about INR20 crore capex per year.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Store additions (250 over FY27-FY28) and FY27 SSG guided at 35-40% (H1 at 38%, Q2 at 46%) point to continued growth, but H1 volume growth was only about 3-37% depending on source and volumes in sub-INR15,000 phones are falling about 15% industry-wide.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Store capex is already committed at about INR20 crore per year for FY27 and FY28, and Chhattisgarh details are due next quarter, but no new capacity beyond the store rollout was announced and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 SSG at 35-40% and H1 revenue growth was 73%, with H2 expected slightly above H1, but no explicit upgrade to revenue or margin guidance was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risk comes from ASP growth slowing to 10-15% next year, gross margin gains being roughly half from lower discounting that may not repeat, and inventory days at 54 vs 46-47 a year ago.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pre-owned (Mobile Exchange Wala) is at 7.3% of Q2 revenue across 108 stores, targeting about 30% penetration by FY29, and accessories (about 5% of revenue) are flagged for scaling, but no specific new product launch date was given.

rows.label: Chhattisgarh details and new state entries
rows.when: next quarter; new state ~1 per year
rows.why: Chhattisgarh operations started in Q3 FY27 with details due next quarter, and Rajasthan, UP and Haryana are flagged as future entries at about one new state per year, though out-of-Maharashtra mix is only 8% in Q2.

rows.label: Interest cost and inventory normalisation
rows.why: Management expects interest cost to fall from 0.6-0.7x toward 0.3-0.4x and inventory days to fall to 46-50 (below 50 by end-Q3) from 54, but the timing depends on IPO proceeds and festive stock unwinding and was discussed loosely.

rows.label: ASP growth slowdown
rows.why: ASP growth is guided to slow from about 33-35% to 10-15% next year, which shifts SSG growth from price to volume and removes a key growth driver.

tone.note: Management was confident on store rollout, SSG and the 750-store target, and more cautious on margin path, with the 6% EBITDA level described as an aspiration; analysts pushed on the Q2 SSG figure, non-Maharashtra share, and the sources of H1 gross margin gains.
